questions.stem: What is the negation of "machine M halts on every input"?
options: M does not halt on every input at once
There is some input on which M does not halt
questions.explain: Negating "for all" gives "there exists", with the condition negated: some input makes M run forever.

questions.stem: Set A is a subset of set B, and x is not in B. What follows?
options: x is in both A and B
questions.explain: Everything in A is also in B. So an element missing from B cannot be in A. This is the reasoning used for nested classes of languages.

questions.stem: Among 20 languages, 12 are in set P, 9 are in set Q and 5 are in both. How many are in neither set?
questions.explain: In P or Q: 12 + 9 − 5 = 16. So 20 − 16 = 4 are in neither.

questions.stem: How many rows does a truth table for 3 variables p, q and r have?
questions.explain: Each variable is true or false, so there are 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 rows.

questions.stem: What does a push-down automaton have that a finite automaton does not?
questions.explain: A PDA is a finite automaton plus a stack. A Turing machine goes further with a read-write tape.

questions.stem: The grammar is S → 0S1 | ε, where ε is the empty string. Which string can it generate?
questions.explain: Applying S → 0S1 twice and then S → ε gives S ⇒ 0S1 ⇒ 00S11 ⇒ 0011. Every string it makes is some 0s followed by the same number of 1s.
